days.theme: Land 20:15, check in, late dinner only
days.why: TV9812 touches down 20:15 and needs 40 min to clear, so you are not out of Shuangliu before ~21:00 and not at the Minyoun Dongda much before 21:45. Nothing ticketed is still open. Deliberately empty: the only thing that belongs here is a late hotpot near the hotel. If anyone still has energy, Taikoo Li / IFS rooftop panda are a 10-minute walk away and the lanes stay lit and open-air late — kept in ideas as an unplanned stroll rather than a scheduled stop.

days.theme: Pandas at opening, teahouse afternoon, opera at night
days.why: One anchor at each end of the day and a tight central cluster in between. Panda Base first because it is genuinely a morning-only activity: gates open 07:30, the animals are active 07:30–09:30 and are asleep in the heat by late morning, so leave the hotel ~06:50 and take the South Gate (pandas are out there at 07:30; the West Gate not until 09:00). 3.5 h on site puts you back downtown for lunch ~11:45. The afternoon is all walkable and all within 1 km: People’s Park (45 min) flows straight into Heming Teahouse inside it (90 min — gaiwan tea and the ear-cleaning ritual, and the one properly restful block of the day), then Kuanzhai Alleys 10 min north for the dusk snack hour (120 min). Sichuan opera closes it: Shufeng Yayun sits in Chengdu Culture Park barely 1 km west of Kuanzhai, show 20:00–21:30, arrive 19:30 — so the fixed evening start costs you no extra transit at all. Stop time ~9.75 h, but two of those hours are seated (teahouse, theatre), so the real walking load is moderate. Chengdu Museum was the cut here — see ideas.

days.theme: Sanxingdui half-day out, Three Kingdoms at dusk
days.why: Sanxingdui eats the whole morning and cannot share a day with another major sight: ~40 km north, so Chengdu East → Guanghan North (18 min on the high-speed train, plus station security) then a 15–20 min taxi, roughly 1.5 h each way on top of 3.5 h on site. Leave the hotel ~07:45, on site ~09:30–13:00, back at Chengdu East ~14:45. Confirmed summer hours 08:30–20:00 (last entry 18:00) 1 Jul–31 Aug, closed Mondays — 21 Aug is a Friday, fine. The afternoon then runs to a single southwest cluster: Wuhou Shrine and Jinli share a wall, so it is one taxi for both. Wuhou 15:15–17:30, Jinli next door from 17:45 into the lantern hour with dinner at the snack stalls. Stop time ~7 h plus ~3 h of travel — a full but not brutal day.

days.theme: 08:30 train from Chengdu East — day is gone
days.why: High-speed departure from Chengdu East at 08:30 with a 60-min buffer means leaving the hotel around 07:00 for breakfast-and-go. Nothing in Chengdu is open, and nothing is worth risking the train for. Legitimately empty.

ideas.name: Chengdu Museum
ideas.why: The hardest cut and the closest call. Free, air-conditioned, genuinely good — but 2.5 h indoors was the most expendable block on day 2, and Sanxingdui tells the ancient-Shu bronze story far better on day 3, so the overlap made it the one to lose. Confirmed Tue–Sun and open to 20:30 in summer (May–Oct), closed Mondays, free but needs online booking 1–3 days ahead. If you want it back: it is on Tianfu Square, five minutes from People’s Park, and the 20:30 closing means it is the natural swap for either the teahouse or Kuanzhai on day 2 — or a rain/heat refuge if the weather turns.

ideas.name: Taikoo Li
ideas.why: Cut as a scheduled stop, not as an experience. It is a 10-minute walk from the Minyoun Dongda, open-air, free and alive late — so it is the one thing that works with no plan at all, including on arrival night if anyone is still standing after check-in. Blocking 90 min for it would have cost a real sight.

ideas.name: Daci Temple
ideas.why: Data-bug casualty. It was tagged Evening, but it is a ticket-checked site that closes 17:30 with last entry 17:00 (the Zen tea area runs to 19:30, the halls do not), and it needs ID / QR registration at the gate. With both full days committed in daylight there is no daytime hour left for it. It sits inside the Taikoo Li block by the hotel, so if a morning frees up it is a 45-min drop-in — but never after dark.

ideas.name: IFS rooftop panda
ideas.why: A 30-minute photo queue for one sculpture, in the same block as Taikoo Li and the hotel. Pure opportunistic add-on — not worth a planned slot when you only have two real days.

ideas.name: SKP Chengdu
ideas.why: Dropped outright. A luxury mall ~14 km south of the hotel, well off every other cluster, and the only argument for it is architecture and air conditioning — both of which Chengdu Museum gives you for free and centrally. The round-trip transit alone would cost most of a Kuanzhai.

ideas.name: Hotpot alt · Shu Daxia
ideas.why: This is a dinner, and you insert meals yourself. Kept as the recommendation for arrival night: it is in the Chunxi Road / Taikoo Li block near the hotel, so it fits the one slot day 1 actually has.

ideas.name: Hotpot alt · Lao Matou
ideas.why: Also a dinner, not a stop. Worth holding as the day-2 or day-3 dinner if you want a shorter queue than Shu Daxia — but check the address before booking, the coordinate in the source data is wrong (see notes).

notes: DATA BUG FIXED — Wuhou Shrine and Daci Temple were both tagged Evening and neither can be. Verified: Wuhou Shrine is 09:00–18:00 with ticket sales stopping at 17:00; Daci Temple is 08:00–17:30 with ticket check ending 17:00. Wuhou is now a daylight stop on day 3 (enter by 15:15 to get a full 2 h); Daci Temple went to ideas because no daylight hour was left for it.

Day 3 hard cutoff: Wuhou Shrine's 17:00 last-ticket is the single fragile point in the whole plan. If the train back from Guanghan slips, Wuhou is the casualty — leave Sanxingdui by 13:30, not later. Jinli is free and open late, so it survives any delay; only the shrine is at risk. Wuhou's Western Garden zone stays open 07:00–22:00 if you arrive too late for the main halls.

Three entries in the source `sights` are structural, not sights, and were excluded from both days and ideas per the no-meals/hotels/stations rule: 'Check in at Minyoun Dongda' (hotel), 'Chengdu East → Guanghan' and 'Guanghan North' (both legs of the Sanxingdui journey, already implied by that stop). All 15 actual sights appear exactly once.

Bookings needed before you fly: Panda Base (online only, opens 14 days ahead — book the earliest morning slot and enter via the South Gate), Sanxingdui Museum, Sichuan opera at Shufeng Yayun, and Chengdu Museum 1–3 days ahead if you reinstate it. Wuhou Shrine and Jinli need no advance booking.

Coordinate error in the source data: 'Hotpot alt · Lao Matou' is listed at 30.4106 / 103.8151, which is ~30 km southwest of the city near Xinjin — but the note says Yulin Middle Road, which is around 30.626 / 104.066. Anything routing off that coordinate will be badly wrong.
Verified closed-days: Sanxingdui closed Mondays, Chengdu Museum closed Mondays. Your days 2 and 3 are Thursday 20 Aug and Friday 21 Aug, so neither is affected.

Sanxingdui is on late-summer hours (08:30–20:00, last entry 18:00, 1 Jul–31 Aug), so a morning slip is recoverable — you could still go in the early afternoon. But doing so kills Wuhou and Jinli, so treat the early start as the plan and the late hours as insurance only.

The heat is the real constraint in late August. Day 2 is deliberately front-loaded (pandas before 11:00) and puts the 13:45–15:15 peak inside a shaded teahouse; day 3 puts the same window on an air-conditioned train back from Guanghan. Neither day asks you to walk in open sun at 14:00.
